summary:
FireRings is an open web application that turns two decades of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning activity calendar. MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) detect fires at different resolutions, so raw records show a false jump when VIIRS begins. With Suomi-NPP data delivery ending in November 2026 and MODIS approaching retirement, this break threatens the long-term fire record.

We harmonize NASA FIRMS hotspots on a common 5.5 km grid, calibrate the sensors on their overlap period, and attach a verified uncertainty range to every value. Users draw any area or pick a place and instantly see which months are critical, which years were worst, and how this month compares with the historical median. A statistical test confirms the sensor break disappears after harmonization.

FireRings is built for emergency responders, land managers and scientists, and also for communities: it works in English, Bangla and Spanish, runs offline, prints a one-page fire almanac, and lets blind users hear the fire season. All code and data products are open source.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FireRings answers three questions for any area on Earth: When is the fire season here? Was this year unusual? Is this month above or below normal? It shows a harmonized burning activity calendar (months × years, 2000 to present), a "Fire Rings" view where each year is a ring like a tree ring, the current month against the historical median, and an alert when the fire season starts earlier than usual. Users can download hotspots and analytics as CSV and charts as PNG.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: NASA FIRMS active fire detections from MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), retrieved through the FIRMS API and archive.

2. Cleaning: per-sensor confidence filters; static industrial sources removed; duplicates removed.

3. Common grid: detections aggregated to 5.5 km cells, counting each cell once per day ("cell-days"), so a 1 km MODIS pixel and several 375 m VIIRS pixels of the same fire are comparable.

4. Harmonization: calibration on the period when both sensors operate, stratified by region, month and land cover, with a gradient-boosted model (XGBoost) benchmarked against a simple ratio baseline.

5. Uncertainty: conformal prediction gives every harmonized value a range with verified coverage of [__]% on years the model never saw.

6. Validation: MODIS–VIIRS agreement improved from [__] (raw) to [__] (harmonized); a changepoint test finds no sensor break after harmonization; [an independent check against NASA EONET wildfire events matched __ of __ events / remove if not done].

7. Explainability: SHAP shows why the sensors disagree (for example, small and low-intensity fires are missed more often by MODIS).

WHY IT MATTERS

Suomi-NPP data delivery ended in November 2026 and MODIS is near the end of its life. Without harmonization, 25 years of fire history cannot be compared with the satellites that continue. Any fire model trained on raw records learns a false upward trend; FireRings provides a consistent record to build on.

WHO IT IS FOR AND INCLUSION

Disaster officers, forest departments, fire services, land managers and researchers. Demonstrated for the Sundarbans and Chittagong Hill Tracts (Bangladesh) and the Paraná Delta and Corrientes (Argentina). Available in English, Bangla and Spanish; works offline; colorblind-safe palettes with icons and text; a screen-reader data table for every chart; "Hear the season" sonification for blind users; a printable one-page fire almanac for places without internet.

TOOLS

Python (polars, DuckDB, scikit-learn, XGBoost, SHAP), React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, D3. Open source under Apache-2.0: [GitHub link].

LIMITATIONS

Satellites cannot see fires under thick cloud or canopy; only Terra-MODIS observed before mid-2002; uncertainty is larger for small areas and for years before VIIRS. The tool supports decisions but does not replace local verification.

USE OF AI TOOLS

Code and text were developed with help from AI assistants (Claude, Claude Code [and Lovable, if used]); all AI-assisted code is acknowledged in the repository (docs/AI_USE.md). All statistics shown in the app are computed by tested code; no AI model generates any displayed number.
